classification.difficultyReason: Establish congruence of four triangles and use corresponding sides to prove that an interior quadrilateral is a rhombus.

content.prompt: The points $P$ and $Q$ are chosen on the diagonal $BD$ of the square $ABCD$ so that $BP=DQ$.

spec.description: Square ABCD with diagonal DB, Q nearer D and P nearer B. Double ticks mark DQ and PB. AP, PC, CQ and QA form the interior quadrilateral. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a square; D,Q,P,B are collinear in this order; DQ=PB. Coordinates specify drawing proportions only and introduce no numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry and equality marks remain visible; no proof conclusions are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that the triangles $ABP$, $CBP$, $ADQ$ and $CDQ$ are all congruent.

answer.worked:
The sides of the square give $AB=CB=AD=CD$. Its diagonal bisects the vertex angles, so
$$\angle ABP=\angle CBP=\angle ADQ=\angle CDQ=45^\circ.$$
Also $BP=DQ$ (given), with $BP$ common to the first two triangles and $DQ$ common to the last two. Thus each triangle has two corresponding sides equal and their included angle equal:
$$\triangle ABP\equiv\triangle CBP\equiv\triangle ADQ\equiv\triangle CDQ\quad\text{(SAS)}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence prove that $APCQ$ is a rhombus.

answer.short: $AP=PC=CQ=QA$ (matching sides of congruent triangles), so $APCQ$ is a rhombus.
answer.worked:
From part a, matching sides of the congruent triangles give
$$AP=CP=AQ=CQ.$$
Thus the four sides of $APCQ$ are equal, so $APCQ$ is a rhombus.
